message: subprocess call uses shell=True with a command string built from a variable. This runs the string through /bin/sh, so shell metacharacters (; | & $() `` ) in the variable are interpreted, not treated as literal text. Use shell=False with an argument list.

os.system() runs its argument through the shell. If any part of the command string is built from a variable, this is OS command injection. Use subprocess.run([...], shell=False) with an argument list instead.

A file path is built by joining a base directory with a variable and then opened. If the variable can contain "../" segments or an absolute path and is not validated/contained beforehand, this is path traversal. Confirm whether the code checks the resolved path stays inside the base directory (e.g. os.path.realpath + os.path.commonpath) before this point.

A SQL query is built with string concatenation ('+') that includes a variable. If any part of that variable is influenced by untrusted input, this is SQL injection. Use parameterized queries instead (cursor.execute(query, params)).
A SQL query is built with an f-string or .format()/％ formatting containing a variable. This interpolates the variable's value directly into SQL syntax. Use parameterized queries instead.
